investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T16:07:32–35Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents, carrying the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the failure occurs at the very first API call — agent creation — no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing a total contract gap for the remote-agent-create check.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 because the eval org has reached its remote agent quota limit of 100. The rejection happens before any agent is provisioned, so the runner never advances past createAgent() and no required evidence is written. All three sibling checks share the identical error message, confirming the failure is rooted in a single shared upstream dependency — the agent creation endpoint — rather than in any individual check's logic or assertion.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T16:07:32–35Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents, carrying the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the failure occurs at the very first API call — agent creation — no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing a total contract gap for the remote-agent-create check.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 because the eval org has reached its remote agent quota limit of 100. The rejection happens before any agent is provisioned, so the runner never advances past createAgent() and no required evidence is written. All three sibling checks share the identical error message, confirming the failure is rooted in a single shared upstream dependency — the agent creation endpoint — rather than in any individual check's logic or assertion.

possibleCauses: Primary (high confidence): The eval org's remote agent count has reached the swarm-enforced hard limit of 100. A prior eval run or external activity created agents that were not cleaned up, exhausting the quota. The 409 error body explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100'.

Secondary (medium confidence): A previous eval run's withCleanup() teardown failed silently, leaving orphaned remote agents in the org and incrementally consuming quota across runs. The verifierContext.history shows previousRunCount=0, meaning no historical pass/fail baseline is available to confirm when quota was first breached.

Tertiary (low confidence): The quota limit of 100 may have been lowered by a platform configuration change, causing previously-passing runs to now exceed the threshold. No evidence of a quota configuration change is present in the supplied artifacts, so this remains speculative.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the same eval run with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents, indicating the swarm backend rejected agent creation because the org-level agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because agent creation is the first step in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1372: createAgent), no downstream evidence—orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message—was ever collected, causing the expected-output contract to be entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval runner. Because the eval probe for remote-agent-runtime calls createAgent as its first substantive action (run-status-probes.mjs line 1372), the 409 terminates the probe before any runtime interaction occurs, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) unpopulated. The same failure hit sibling checks remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state with the identical error message, confirming the quota condition is the shared upstream blocker for the entire remote-agents feature eval suite. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — org-level swarm agent quota exhausted: the eval service account's org has accumulated 100 remote agents (the stated limit) and the swarm backend refuses further creation. Prior eval runs or leaked agents from incomplete cleanup (withCleanup failures) may have consumed the quota.

Secondary — eval cleanup not completing: the runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1370) to delete agents after each run. If cleanup failed in prior runs, orphaned agents could have accumulated against the quota even though no passing run history is recorded (previousRunCount=0 in verifier history).

Tertiary — eval service account quota misconfiguration: the quota limit of 100 may be set too low for the eval org, or the eval org is shared with non-eval workloads that have consumed quota independently.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on /api/generate/image/stream in production-api
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint was unreachable at the time of the probe. Because the stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame, both required contract assertions failed: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1438) and received a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error with error code indicating "agent runtime endpoint not found (404)". The harness backing the production-api runtime environment was either not deployed, deployed at a different URL than the one configured via LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL, or running an incompatible version that does not expose the expected endpoint. This is an eval infrastructure / harness connectivity failure localized to the production-api runtime target; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the packet.
proof: failed-check.evidence: stream emitted frames [generation_start, generation_error, message]; generation_error frame carries code=SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message='agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'
